why: A (universes 0): for a slice submanifold N of a Euclidean V with the induced connection (DX/dt = P X'), two parallel fields along any curve have constant inner product (i.e. the induced connection IS compatible), and for smooth c the project's parallelTransport T_{c(t₀)}N ≃ₗᵢ T_{c(t₁)}N preserves inner products, is the identity at t₀ = t₁ and is transitive. B: on an abstract manifold with a smooth Riemannian metric and an ARBITRARY smooth Mathlib connection ASSUMED compatible (Milnor's definition), parallel translation P_{t₀} ↦ P_t is given by a linear isometry equivalence. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: A's objects are embedded and its connection is the induced one; B needs Lemmas 8.1/8.2 for an arbitrary connection on an abstract manifold (existence/uniqueness of parallel fields via Christoffel symbols and coordinate patching — 'not formalized' per Connection.lean) to make P_{t₀} ↦ P_t a well-defined surjective linear map; Whitney embedding does not help since B's connection is not the induced one. B ⇒ A fails: B takes compatibility as a hypothesis, while A proves that the induced connection is compatible (IsParallel.inner_eq) and constructs the transport on N; B's abstract objects are not the project's. A could be re-proved outright, but parallelTransport's own body uses the banned IsParallel.inner_eq, so even a vacuous B ⇒ A would need an A' with that proof abstracted; not attempted.
embedded_special_case_note: Items/V6_9.lean: B_emb := B for M = Bridge.Sub hN (↥N, model ℝⁿ, induced metric) and cov = Bridge.conn; B_to_B_emb is a genuine instance (Bridge.conn_contMDiff; B's IsCompatibleMetric for conn from Bridge.conn_isCompat on s = univ). Dictionary (namespace Emb, glue from Items/V6_6.lean plus isParallel_iff as in V6_8): B's parallel fields along a smooth curve = smooth project-parallel fields read in V; Emb.eT : T_x(↥N) ≃ₗ tangentSubspace hN x, an isometry by Bridge.norm_eq. Proved B_emb ⇔ A89 := (for model ℝⁿ and SMOOTH c) project-parallel fields have constant inner products ∧ inner_parallelTransport. A89 ⇒ B_emb: L := eT ≫ (parallelTransport).toLinearEquiv ≫ eT⁻¹, with the isometry proved from A89's inner_parallelTransport clause (not from parallelTransport's own norm_map'), and L(P t₀) = P t by IsParallel.eq_parallelField. B_emb ⇒ A89: B's isometry gives ⟨P,P'⟩ constant; inner_parallelTransport follows via parallelTransport_apply (rfl) and parallelField_spec. Hence A_to_B_emb (uses A) and B_to_A89 (uses B), both #rt_check_soft OK with review: IsParallel.inner_eq is reached only through the norm_map' proof field of Morse.parallelTransportL, because A (and A89) mention Morse.parallelTransport; neither proof uses that field. What A has beyond B_emb: arbitrary model Z, constancy of inner products along NON-smooth curves (IsParallel.inner_eq has no smoothness hypothesis on c), and parallelTransport_self / parallelTransport_trans (properties of the project's construction, not in B's existential). Limitation: only the induced connection, not every compatible connection on ↥N.
